title: Linear Queue Using Arrays
definition: A Queue is a linear data structure that operates under the FIFO (First In, First Out) principle, where elements are inserted at the back end (rear) and removed from the front end (front).
fifo_principle: The element that enters first is the first to be serviced and leave. Real-world analogy: People standing in a ticket counter queue or a printer document job spooler.
dry_run: enqueue(60): rear == 4 (MAX-1) is TRUE -> Queue Overflow is reported even though index 0 is empty!
linear_queue_limitation: The major drawback of a linear array queue is FALSE OVERFLOW (memory waste). When elements are dequeued, the front pointer moves forward, leaving unused vacant slots at the front of the array. Even if slots 0, 1, 2 are empty, if rear == MAX - 1, no new elements can be enqueued. This limitation directly necessitates Circular Queues.
applications: CPU Scheduling: Ready queue in multiprogramming operating systems (e.g. Round Robin, FCFS).
Print Spooling: Printing documents in the exact order submitted.
Graph Traversal: Breadth-First Search (BFS) uses a queue to visit vertices level by level.
Buffering: Real-time asynchronous data buffers (e.g., keyboard keystrokes buffer, network socket packet buffers).

viva_questions.question: What is false overflow in a linear queue?
viva_questions.answer: False overflow occurs when the rear pointer reaches MAX - 1, triggering an overflow error, even though elements were previously dequeued and empty slots exist at the front of the array.

viva_questions.question: How can false overflow be resolved without shifting array elements?
viva_questions.answer: By using a Circular Queue, where the rear wraps around to index 0 using the modulo operator: '(rear + 1) % MAX'.
